hook.line: Someone asks you something so obvious that a calm answer would sound cold. Spanish has a few small moves for answering with feeling, and Tomás needs them the moment Vale asks about her pastries.
hook.en: Do I like it? I love it!

examples.en: But I already told you! (to a friend)
Do I like it? I love it!
Am I tired? Not at all! (a man speaking)
But Vale cooks better than anyone!

examples.es: ¿Que si quiero más café? ¡Pues claro que quiero!
examples.en: Do I want more coffee? Of course I do!

rule:
Three small moves.

1. *¡Si…!* at the start of a sentence is not "if". It means "but, come on", and you use it to protest or defend: *¡Si ya te lo dije!* The verb stays plain.
2. *¿Que si…?* repeats the question you were asked, as "Do I…?", before you answer it with force: *¿Que si me gusta? ¡Me encanta!*
3. *¡Pues claro que…!* is "of course", and the verb follows as usual: *¡Pues claro que voy!* For "of course not", put *no* right after *que*.

*¡Qué va!* on its own means "not at all". It is always a no.
smallPrint: Teachers call these emphatic structures: the *si* is the emphatic *si*, and *que si* is an echo question.

readAndPick.es: ¿Que si sé quién es? ¡Pues claro que sé!
options: Do I know who he is? Of course I do!
Does he know who I am? Of course!
I don't know who he is.

readAndPick.es: ¿Que si te ayudo? ¡Pues claro que te ayudo!
options: Did I help you? Of course I did!
Will I help you? Of course I'll help you!
Will you help me? Of course you will!

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *voy* or *fui* and type the whole sentence: Of course I'm going! *¡Pues claro que ___!*
yourTurn.why: You are going now, so the plain present, *voy*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: But I already told you!
yourTurn.why: A bare *si* at the start protests, like "but".

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Do I like it? I love it!
yourTurn.why: *Que si* repeats the question, then you answer.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, a man speaking: Am I tired? Not at all!
yourTurn.why: *Qué va* is the "not at all" answer.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *¡Pues claro que voy!* Say: Of course I'm not going!
Type in Spanish: But Vale cooks better than anyone!
accept: ¡Pero si Vale cocina mejor que todos!

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Will I help you? Of course I'll help you!
yourTurn.answer: ¿Que si te ayudo? ¡Pues claro que te ayudo!
yourTurn.why: Echo the question with *que si*, then answer with *pues claro que*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. This *si* is not "yes", so it has no accent.
Almost. To repeat the question you were asked, Spanish needs *que* before *si*.
Almost. For "I'm going", use the present, *voy*; *fui* means "I went".

pitfalls.wrong: ¿Que si me gusta? ¡Qué va, me encanta!
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Qué va* always means "not at all", so it can't go before a yes.

personal: Think of something people always ask you, and answer it with force: *¿Que si…?* then *¡Pues claro que…!*
